svg.title: Unassigned motion dialects: one-cell pressure studies
svg.desc: Research-only native-vector comparison. Every row fixes its centerline, endpoints and direction. Thin fallback loses pattern identity. Size samples are not production readability validation.

g.text: NEW MOTION PROPOSAL / RESEARCH ONLY / ONE-CELL GEOMETRY
One common path per row: same A→B direction and endpoints. Pressure changes; black area is not equalized.
No character assignment, action trajectory or ability claim. The open-core motif is a candidate vocabulary, not an adopted mark.
One open cavity · one return · unequal shoulders
2. Broaden the back and long shoulder.
3. Add one soft inner pressure lobe.
4. Taper both ends; leave the side open.
Rounded mass and a readable return.
Heavier; can resemble a curled sign.
Same narrow path; uniform line weight.
One continuous ribbon; local pressure lobe.
The core becomes unstable when reduced.
Pattern identity lost; no ability restriction implied.
64 px: the return is no longer

3. Keep one local pressure lobe only.
4. If the core collapses, remove the lobe.

This is a local geometry test, not a cap
on a character’s line count or abilities.
One dominant corner; no all-over serration.

Less fluid; may read as a graphic sign.
128 / 64 px = sample viewport width in this 1× PNG. High-contrast display examples only; not game/TV readability tests or final resolution targets.
